One of the most important things students learn in econometrics classes is that *correlation is not causation*. This is a central insight which needs to be carefully considered when interpreting the results of a statistical model. Since the 1980s there is a growing literature on how to incorporate causal relationships in empirical applications, which often involve Bayesian networks.[^pearl] This post provides an introduction to Bayesian networks and how they can be used in R.

Bayesian networks were deveolped in the early 1980s when artificial inteligences (AI) was in its early stages.

Bayesian networks are even used in every smartphone to 

Bayesian models seem to be much more in line with the process of human learning, which is always a mixture of prior belief that is updated with every new experience.
